text: What is doeff? Algebraic effects for Python.
A program yields effects. A handler receives each one together with k, the rest of the program.
What the handler does with k decides what the effect means.
research yields one Spend per topic. It knows nothing about what spending means.
free answers each Spend and lets the rest run. Notes on both topics.
refuse drops k at the first Spend. research stops there.
A budget keeps what is left between effects. With ten, both Spends fit.
With five, only two is left for the second Spend. The budget drops k.
Handlers stack. trace takes every effect first, notes it, and passes it on to the budget.
State, exceptions, concurrency, observation and I/O are effects of this same kind.
crawl fetches pages in parallel tasks, counts them in state, and logs each fetch.
Each effect travels out to the handler that gives it its meaning.
The empty page raises in its task. Try turns the error into a value.
size, crawl and report name the effects they need. Where they run decides the handlers.
Swapping I/O is one use. A handler that calls the network answers Fetch, and the code stays as it is.
Leave the Fetch handler out, and nobody answers: each task gets an unhandled effect.
It is one use, not what doeff is. research does no I/O at all.
Its limits. Continuations are one-shot: each k resumes at most once.
Resume k for tea, then again for coffee, and the second Resume raises a RuntimeError.
What stands in for it: run the whole program again, once per choice. A program is a value.
Effects are not in the types. A missing handler shows only when the program runs.
And an effect costs a few microseconds. Nothing next to I/O, but visible in a tight loop.
Next to other effect systems: in effect and effectful, a handler never gets the continuation.
OCaml 5 is the closest: one-shot continuations, and no effects in the types.
Koka resumes many times, and checks effects in its types. doeff has neither.
doeff: algebraic effects for Python. Your code yields effects, and handlers decide what they mean.
